Permissions updated to rwxr-xr-x. Better - not writable by others. (700 is tighter since only root needs it.)
Refused in this simulation: 777 makes files writable by everyone - the opposite of the fix.

reflection: Why is a world-writable script run by root via cron critical?
Which SUID binaries are normal on Ubuntu?
How would you prevent this regressing?
solution: SUID list contains /usr/local/bin/sysinfo (unexpected, owned by root). World-writable: /opt/backup/backup.sh (run by root cron). Fix: chmod 700 and chown root:root; remove SUID from sysinfo after confirming with owners.
defensive: Detect with scheduled permission audits (find), file integrity monitoring on scripts executed by root, and configuration management enforcing modes. Restrict cron scripts to root-owned, non-writable paths.

options: World-writable script executed by root cron
questions.explain: Any user could inject commands that run as root.
Owner rwx, group and others none.
